Extrait de Parfum. The inspiration for this potent aquatic floral is Nāmaka, the sacred Hawaiian goddess of sea and waves, sister of the tempestuous Pele, goddess of fire and volcanic turbulence. Hawaiian legends tell of the eternal cycle of conflict between oceanic Nāmaka and the blazing rage of Pele. Studio Tanaïs has captured both the paradise and the power.. At the heart of Nāmaka is monoï, the evocative and transportive scent of tiare buds hand-picked early in the morning and macerated in coconut oil. We are familiar with its luscious, oily velveteen perfume from sun protection creams and post-sun oils, but true monoï is prohibitively expensive and rare to find outside niche perfumery. Nāmaka is suffused with it: an ivory bouquet of tiare flowers, thick with heady scent, laid upon waves as offerings. The tiare carries an addictive erotic ripeness with hints of vanillic tonka and coumarin, its decadence deliciously aphrodisiac and moreish.. Mimosa Olessence brings a more pronounced anisic note to the composition, produced by a lower temperature extraction process that many perfumers consider a truer representation of mimosa than other absolutes. Plumeria adds a further plush dimension with its hints of peachy citrus, gardenia and clove. Creamy coconut milk, jasmine and a delicious amber accord complete the floral body, assembled to honour the paradise birthplace of sacred Nāmaka.. A marine accord underpins everything, both briny and lactonic, refreshing and a little ominous. Then there is choya nak, the strange result of roasting seashells with sandalwood, producing a compelling scent of atramental ocean that exalts the marine accord and tempers the lavish tiare flowers.. Nāmaka has huge solar projection, the familiarity of monoï boosting our attraction to it. Studio Tanaïs has created a beautifully addictive perfume of considerable power, a vast oceanic floral with impressive longevity. If you close your eyes, you can smell the crashing waves, tossing flower garlands in eddies of blue and white foam, nights of indolic blooms suffusing the air.. . Composition: . Egyptian Neroli, Marine Accord, White Grapefruit. Tiare Flower, Mimosa Olessence, Coconut Milk, Jasmine Sambac, Plumeria Petal. Eucalyptus Absolute, Nutmeg, Botanical Ambergris, Roasted Seashell. . inci list: Organic Cane Alcohol, isopropyl myristate, essential oils, resins, absolutes, fine fragrance raw materials .

Extrait de Parfum. “Sacred notes of palo santo, wild white sage, and black copal, are the incenses of the Americas, burned in ceremony for protection and clarity; as oils they smell as cool as the desert night.” . Tanaïs, “Mojave,” In Sensorium: Notes For My People . In many ways, Mojave is a call for rain, a scented hymn rising on hot air to the skies, beseeching water to fall on parched skin. The three key notes of copal, mitti attar and white sage form a muscular triangle around which the other notes drift in and out of desert consciousness.. Copal is an immersive ritualistic incense associated with ceremonial rites, channelling prayers and spirits. Its odour is dense and dusky, shadowy fumes with a bittersweet throatiness. Tanaïs has allied the copal to mitti attar, the eerie scent of metallic rain falling on parched earth, and the smudge-stick ambience of white sage, a sacred material used for millennia to cleanse and purify.. Eucalyptus and an oceanic tang from the collision of smoke and mitti's rain motif create an uneasy balance within Mojave. Will rain fall and water the waiting land or pass through? This anticipation is the pungent and thought-provoking mood of Mojave.. Careworn leather and honeyed lime blossom form an offbeat heart with the addition of palo santo, another smoky wood, enhanced with just the right dose of oud and amber in an elegant late-developing base. Mojave is a fascinating composition to wear, delirious and sparse at the same time.. . Composition: . Sacred Black Copal, Wildcrafted White Sage, Eucalyptus Blue Maille, Juniper Leaf. Leather Accord, Linden Blossom, Palo Santo. Mitti Attar, Sandalwood, Aloeswood, Animalic Amber. . Organic Cane Alcohol, isopropyl myristate, essential oils, resins, absolutes, fine fragrance raw materials .

Extrait de Parfum. Matí is a homeland scent, made from monsoon rain soaked clays distilled in sandalwood, sourced from Kannauj. Each batch of Matí is ephemeral, a memory of that particular monsoon season.. In Tanaïs's mother’s village, little terracotta bricks were a snack for expecting mothers, tiny pieces of earth chocolate. Betel leaf, the spicy green note of their grandmother’s beloved after dinner treat, paan, is the heart of this composition, an ode to their foremothers.. Each batch of Matí is distinct and different, as the Ganges Mitti Attar at its heart is specific to the time, monsoon and scent of clay that it is distilled. The current batch is Matí 2.0.. “Mati held the scent of their motherland, Purba Bengal, East Bengal, ancestral Bengal. When they tasted matí for the last time, they absorbed the essence of desh…They knew they might never return home again, so they settled for the memory of the earth, rain-wetted matí on their tongues.”. —Tanaïs, “Mati,” In Sensorium: Notes For My People. . Composition: . Rose Petals, Pink Peppercorn, Timur Pepper. Betel Leaf, Roasted Cocoa, Jasmine Sambac, Rose Attar, Turkish Rose. Ganges Mitti Attar, Ruh Khus (Wild Green Vetiver) Attar, Wet Soil, Musk, Tonka Bean, Vanilla, Sylheti Oud. . inci list: Organic Cane Alcohol, isopropyl myristate, essential oils, resins, absolutes, fine fragrance raw materials .

Extrait de Parfum. “When I returned to New York, I missed my old [New Delhi] haunts and scents of the little Gold Leaf cigarettes I smoked, tea, spices, garlands of rose, carnation and marigold dangling from the wedding shops, so I recreated that place in this perfume, Mala, as in, a garland of flowers, beads, and stories; in Spanish, a bad woman. I use a single drop of scent of a loose woman°—choya nakh oil—to fix the perfume, so it lingers.” . —Tanaïs, “Mala,” In Sensorium: Notes for My People . Inspired by flower garlands threaded for rituals commemorating life, love and death in New Delhi, with swirls of temple incense, saffron and henna. Mala is a memory scent, a forceful blend honouring Tanaïs' nostalgia for Delhi, its abundant flora and the thrills of glorious sin. Woven hazily through the composition is the smoke of narcotic tobacco, the papery, spiced odour of those Gold Leaf cigarettes, renowned for their ability to permeate and linger in hair and on fabric.. The scent of sea stones and beach fire flows in and out of Mala, achieved with choya nakh, a rare attar made by roasting shells of particular molluscs at high temperatures. The result is utterly unique: salt and the ashes of charred shells. Incredibly potent, requiring only a tiny drop to fix a perfume, choya nakh is Tanaïs' essence of the bad woman: the note that makes Mala not only transport but imprint on your senses.. . Composition: . Clary Sage, Saffron, Rose Essence. Coriander, Rose Maroc, Marigold Attar, Carnation Essence, Cardamom. Tagetes Absolute, Nag Champa Incense Accord, Sandalwood, Choya Nakh (Roasted Seashell), Tobacco Absolute. . inci list: organic cane alcohol, isopropyl myristate, essential oils, resins, absolutes, fine fragrance raw materials .

Faux Rose slyly suggests a certain plasticity and gaudiness and this concept is sensually exalted with a moreish honeycomb effect and the unusual addition of a delicious patisserie accord inspired by Pan di Spagna, the classic Italian cake made with just three ingredients, flour, eggs and sugar. Eau de Parfum. . Renaissance. Nacreous palazzos. A dormeuse against an egg-shell blue wall… pearls, gold, marble. A setting for pale sun-shy skin. Silks fluttered by sea-tinted breezes. Jasmine flowers crushed beneath slumbering bodies in a gilded bed, decorated with scallops and abalone pearls. A Murano chandelier catches the shifting light, flickering light around the room.. Viva Maria conjures all of this to the soundtrack of Madonna’s Like A Virgin as she shimmers at the peak of her beauty in lace on a gondola and trails wedding whites through chiaroscuro rooms. The fantasy and ache of Viva Maria is beautifully realised, focussed on the indolic thrill of jasmine, that combination of white solar gloss and animalic allure. The perfume explores the dichotomy of Madonna/whore, goddess mother, the two Mary’s in the story of Christ. This is something Madonna Ciccone has been exploring her entire visual and musical career.. The jasmine is the centrepiece but around it are fascinating elements that wrap and play with the evolution of the flower’s sensuality. A squeeze of bergamot in the top notes served to sharpen any potential over-sweetness and Amelia has used Fichi D’India, or prickly pear as it more commonly known, to introduce a delicious moist note with watermelon and pear facets. It is an unusual and uplifting note that is exalted superbly by a wash of crushed seashells and ambergris, both elemental oceanic notes. More often than not, the seashell note has a pungent seared personality but here it is softly nostalgic and a perfect counterpoint to the pearlescent floral mood.. Viva Maria is vivacious, intelligent perfumery that uses materials to conjure a distinctive mood of slumbering grace and the fires within.. Eau de Parfum. This rococo-inspired perfume shimmers with playful seduction, erotic frivolity embroidered with powdered insouciance and giddy Versailles cosplay. Dauphine is a sublime homage to Marie Antoinette, the doomed Austrian-born queen married to Louis XVI, whose decorative lives played out in opulence and ignorance and ended on the guillotine during the bloody carnage of the French Revolution. Loved and loathed in equal measure, she was someone who even now causes heated debate. Her enclosed existence at Versailles unfolded in a succession of artificial gardens, role-playing, balls, perfume, affairs, jewels and extraordinary fashion.. Scent played an important role in the life of the Queen, she used a perfumer called Jean-Louis Fargeon who created flower-centric compositions for her, a huge departure from the heavier musk and attar based compositions that had held sway for centuries. The coquettish whimsy that soundtracks Dauphine is its beguiling strength.. Dauphine is floated on a silken ribboning of pastel-mood lilacs, hints of almond, jasmine and cut cucumber. Always thought of the essential scent of Spring, the dense honey-tinted panicles exuding a pungent unique perfume. Marie Antoinette had a passion for pastel colours, a fashion that hugely influenced the fickle royal court. So, this lilac note is a perfect theme, complimented by a blush of apricot and just the right amount of bittersweet bergamot. Clove exalts the lilac and ambrette brings powdered musky romance. A delicious hush of satin musks drape delicately over the perfume, enhancing and prolonging the rococo beauty of this most singular scent.. Composition: . Bergamot, Apricot. Pastel Lilacs, Clove. Eau de Parfum. . Philosopher’s Walk is the fourth release from Eugen Nizac’s emotional and profoundly beautiful brand Les Abstraits. Each perfume, created in collaboration with Master Perfumer Antoine Lie, is a meticulous and complex melange of materials and ideas. They smell divine.. Lie has used the Grand Cru palette of natural materials, an haute level collection of absolutes from around the globe subject to three strict principles that provide an exceptionally powerful range of ingredients.. Lie has always had a magical ability to understand the nuances and differing personalities of notes and how they blend, often subverting expectations of what is possible in perfumery. He is a resolutely modern, almost brutalist perfumer. It's possible to think about him in terms of someone who chooses to renovate a classic architectural project by grafting on something startling and seemingly inappropriate but then you realise the organic movement from style to style is genius. Lie likes to remind us of perfumes tropes and tendencies through time and then hone, cut, weave and engineer blocks, bolts and materials onto them, allowing us to experience vintage echoes refracted through an expert modern eye.. Philosopher’s Walk is no exception, in fact it is a fabulously rendered exemplar of how Lie works, filtering a classic barbershop fougère through an eerie gauze of alien floral beauty. Perfect for both men and women due to its ambiguity and skilled coalescence of concepts. It is a judiciously assembled smoky floral, hazy with delicate powder, drifting over lavender fields, coming slowly to life under dawn-bruised skies.. Philosopher’s Walk has distinctive elements that reflect the craftsmanship of grooming. The steam from hot towels placed on the face to soften the skin, frothy shaving soap and the finest grade talc to further soothe and dry the skin. A classic and hugely popular lotion was Pinard-Clubman with notes of orange, lemon, jasmine, lavender, musks and woods like pine or sandalwood. All of which are echoed throughout Philosopher’s Walk.. An intriguing edition is costus, a root that adds a dirty ginger animalic vibe of unwashed hair and fur. This might sound a tad gross, but used as it is here with discretion, it creates a beautiful tension with the powdered dusting of violet and carnation, sparking memories of washed and cut hair in barber shops. Geranium, sparkling pink pepper, orange blossom, juniper and an aromatic Ceylonese cinnamon absolute further enhance the intricate plotting of notes.. Despite its classically masculine coding, Philosopher’s Walk is most definitely a perfume for everyone, the joyous barbershop aspects blend seamlessly with a floral sensuality, it is both gauze and garment, blurred and nostalgic. Yet Lie and Eugen have succeeded in making an eau de parfum that smells sharply modern, tapping into distant dreams and memories.. . Composition . Eau de Parfum. . “It appears that the loss of the scent of Monkeyflower was first noticed in Britain in 1909, when a well-known nurseryman asked: 'Is there such a thing now as a common Musk with the old Musk perfume?” . – THE LOST FRAGRANCE OF MUSK, letter published in the journal Nature, 1934. . What a curious perfume Monkeyflower is, but one would expect nothing less from innovative Swedish perfume collective, Stora Skuggan. Each of their fragrances to date has been fascinating and beautiful, with carefully delineated structures and unique ingredients.. In essence Monkeyflower is homage to a flower that mysteriously lost its scent. Coltsfoot, with its bright yellow flowers, was also known as Tussilago and often used in herbal concoctions, but under extreme caution due to dangerous alkaloids lurking in its innocent looking foliage. It had an earthy, meadow sweet muskiness with a dry herbaceous aura.. An intriguing sunscreen note opens the perfume with the xanthous Coltsfoot, adding a warm creamy solar indolence to proceedings. These two notes set a moreish scene for further yellow sunny materials like buttercup, chamomile and the always strange Goldenberry or Physalis as it is more commonly named.. The base is a field of hay, ready for harvest, gilded and tinged with an ephemeral tobacco leaf vibe. Monkeyflower on the skin is subtle but quietly sensational, a slowburn of musky desiccation laced with honey and smears of wild blossom pollen. There is a sense of nostalgia too, a hint of something lost, fitting for a perfume honouring a vanished aroma.. . Composition: . Tussilago, Sunscreen. Fig Buttercup, Chamomile Goldberry. Musk, Hay. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum, aqua, hydroxycitronellal, alpha-isomethyl ionone, limonene, benzyl salicylate, linalool, citronellol, eugenol, geraniol .

listings.description: Eau de Parfum. . François Boucher’s flushed and suggestive L’Odalisque is Miskeo’s inspiration for Portrait de Madame et Son Chat, a painting of overt sensuality, blushing skin and voluptuous indolence. Powder blues, silks flowing like water around a satiated nude on a chaise longue, a piece of furniture that seems designed purely for come hither posturing. L’Odalisque is swathed in costly fabrics, textures contrasting against the aroused pink of her skin and a choker of exquisite pearls.. Portrait de Madame et Son Chat is a beautiful and beguiling perfume, a study in fleshy enigma and muted boudoir ambience. Sevres blue, Pompadour pink, dove grey and buttercup yellow are the hues served up in swooning perfumed deshabille. As is often seen in Rococo art, the rooms and furniture are more dressed than the skin and bodies of the women.. This portrait is one deliberate effect and undertones of pearlescent exhibitionism. A fur accord is the purring Persian cat beneath the hand, musks evoke the fabric strewn room and chill of pearls that need body heat to give them heat. An unexpected note of toasted corn chips seems anomalous but is in fact pitch perfect, bringing a delicious warm, gourmand skin tone to the mix. A gentle undulation of amber floats up as the scent opens, suggesting a dreamy informality beneath the rigidity of societal norms.. Portrait de Madame et Son Chat is fascinating, a plush melange of delicate materials made tender by its stylish exploration of the tensions between the studied frivolity of rococo, whilst not ignoring the deliberate loosening of bodices as flesh becomes weapon and decoration.. . listings.description: Eau de Parfum. . Still Life with Apples. The translation is simple enough. The French words nature morte literally mean dead nature, which in many ways adds a deeply melancholic memento mori vibe to proceedings. During the Dutch Golden Age of flower painting, the blooms were often accompanied by symbols of mortality, rotting apples, insects, clocks, hourglasses and snuffed out candles.. Nature Morte avec Pommes is a distinctive perfume, chewy, animalic, yeasty and fruity. First impressions are puzzling, but the notes come together with wit and sensuality with hints of roasted barley, caramelised cereals, home brew cider and broken bread. Nature Morte avec Pommes smells delicately autumnal and gustatory, with threads of gold, oaken circlets and scattered ripe red apples woven in and out of an ornate table tableau with goblets of pale wine, faded blue Sèvres vessels overflowing with whole and shattered walnuts and glazed breads.. What makes Nature Morte avec Pommes so fascinating to wear is the fact that Miskeo has dared to render the effects of time passing amid lush and dazzling painted blooms. A chilled white wine note suggests chalky cellars and a hint of damp while tonka bean provides a delicate vanillic smoke counterpoint to the plush stickiness and painterly intrigue of the gourmand threads.. . Eau de Parfum. . This giddy, coquettish perfume bubbles with bittersweet summer blush. An allegory is defined as a painting, poem or other piece of writing that can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, more often than not political, moral or religious. This seemingly innocent, orange-flushed perfume uses sparkling aldehydes to suggest sunlight flickering in a summer garden, warmed by cinnamon and the sunbaked liquorice nuances of immortelle.. The capricious vibe is further enhanced by a witty use of a Chinotto note in the bright head notes. Chinotto is horticulturally citrus myrtifolia, a small dark orange from the myrtle-leaved orange tree but is also the name for a popular carbonated drink in Italy and Malta. Similar to Coca Cola in its deep caramelised hue, it has a distinctive pithy bitterness underpinning the sweetness. In Allégorie de L’Eté the Chinotto note, both dark bitter fruit and fizzy fun play a part in aerating the other notes, complimenting anisic fennel and the grassy tobacco hint of hay.. Jean Honoré Fragonard’s famous painting The Swing is called L’Escarpolette or Les Hasards Heureux de L’Escarpolette, which sounds infinitely better than the English translation Lucky Accidents of the Swing. Strictly speaking, Escarpolette is a garden swing, one with ropes. And in Fragonard’s delicious pretty painting, a young woman wearing frothy pink silks swings high and her slipper is seen to be flying through the air in a sensual blooming garden over the head of a young man reclining on the ground.. There is little mystery in where his eyes are focussed, and this gives the painting a frisson of naughty assignation or voyeurism. On the right, in shadow is an older man, perhaps her cuckolded husband or a member of clergy, looking on with a mix of disapproval and attraction.. In many ways Allégorie de L’Eté is the lush embodiment of L’Escarpolette, an artwork that scandalised contemporaries. The fabrics, shades of pink, the fertile garden, crimson swing seat, blushing skin and suggestion of wrong-doing in Eden reflect the stylised flightiness of Miskeo’s perfume. The perfume is beautiful to wear, a perfect blend of melting summer and a darker, more bittersweet exhilaration.. . Composition . Chinotto, Aldehyde. Immortelle, Cinnamon. Labdanum, Fennel, Hay. Eau de Parfum. . Thumbsucker is inspired by the ancient tale of an Indian King called Yuvanashva, who despite his wealth and power had no male heir. The priests and high officials created a blessed holy water that would be drunk by the queen, boosting her chances of having a boy child. After a long blessing ceremony, the King fell asleep. He woke with a raging thirst and seeing the container full of water, drank every drop. Unease settled through the court, and it was discovered the King was pregnant. The baby was delivered through a hole cut into his side and according to legend Indra the King of Gods attended the unique birth, cut a gash in his thumb, feeding the infant holy milk from his wound.. Tendrils of honeyed animalic woods and styrax resin fume through Thumbsucker, while a dusting of boudoir violet and a lick of boozy cherry shape an unexpected, compelling beauty. A realistic beeswax note imparts a feral sweetness, complimenting the honey and suggesting raw hive wax mixed with bee pheromones, royal jelly, old wood and propolis.. There is no denying the oddity of Thumbsucker, this is due in part to the fatty cold candle wax and bitter almond duo that anchor the scent. The other keynote is the swooning decadence of narcissus, a hypnotic bloom of death and dizzying beauty, forever a flower of dream, narcosis and decadence. It spreads through Thumbsucker like an opiate, numbing and exalting as it does. Narcissus is necessary to counterpoint any bitterness and lifts the bee and candle wax.. The mix of cold, dry and compulsive fluctuations within Thumbsucker make it fascinating to wear.. . Composition: . Honey, Narcissus. Violet, Cherry. Eau de Parfum. . This beguiling scent is Stora Skuggan’s rendition of Silphium (Laserwort/Laser) a renowned botanical herb, now extinct but in Roman times was as valuable as gold due to its unique gustatory flavour and use in medicines and aphrodisiacs, as a preservative and in animal feed. It was native to Cyrene, located in modern day Libya. Not a particularly beautiful plant, but as with many things, the true beauty and treasure lay within, in this case a pungent aromatic sap dried used in its multifarious ways.. Silphium is gloriously eccentric and out of time. A doomed herbaceous thing of textural originality. It is one thing to want to recreate something, but another thing altogether to make it so beautifully wearable. . A delicately calibrated silphium accord of rubbed and slightly sulphurous green opens the perfume, combined with geranium, zesty ginger, clove and the ambergris insouciance of gum cistus. This also functions as a fixative, holding deepening traces of the accord throughout the drydown.. The chill spikes of the top notes cede to tobacco and cinnamon. It is the atmospheric mingle of medicinal and culinary that creates soft tension within Silphium.. Fumes of frankincense, malleable leather and woods rise from the base and provide a soft gentle ending. It is a tricky perfume to classify and that is perhaps the point, the echo of a Roman past filtered through the contemporary lens of hip Swedes.. . Composition: . Silphium Accord, Cistus. It is simply pine; top, heart and base; but fascinatingly, it is not the piney tarred turpentine hit you might expect. Pine raises the ghosts of Nordic black churches, wood seared, ornate and mysterious, in flames during the infamous Black Metal Church Burnings in the 90’s. Eau de Parfum. . This wonderfully titled perfume has its origins in spelunking, more commonly known as caving.. 'At night, the moon shines into the cave so brightly the light itself seems to take form, like a mist. It gathers in the ceiling and makes the limestone stalactites glitter and gleam, dripping tears of white liquid into puddles on the rock floor that never dries. Moonmilk.' . These words from Conrad Gessner, a Swiss 16th century scientific polymath displayed his passion for spelunking in an article entitled In 1555 he published his narrative Descriptio Montis Fracti sive Montis Pilati about an excursion to the Gnepfstein mountain in the Emmental Alpine region. It was there he experienced for the first time the eerie opaque white exudation of limestone precipitate that coated walls and dripped like luminous celestial milk.. Moonmilk, in many ways reflects the sensual gawky nudity of American photographer Ryan McGinley, one of the most celebrated chroniclers of the alternative lifestyles. McGinley actually published a collection of photographs entitled Moonmillk, with his trademark angular beautiful folk set inside a spectacular cave system. Boy and Girl flesh glows, echoing the moonmilk that fascinated Gessner.. The perfume is a composed mood of granular milkiness, like cold weather barely dissolved in a suspension of black tea, piquant lime, spice-painted flowers and creamy Mysore sandalwood. The steady, softness of the drydown conjures up the hypnotic drip of limestone whiteness, the damp chalkiness of it filling the subterranean air.. The geological nuances of Moonmilk are unique. It is rare to find a scent that translates its inspirations quite so persuasively and with such a sigh of nuanced awe.. The use of black tea is deviceful, a tannic touch of swirling milky beverage enhanced by green cardamom and black pepper, hints of creamy lily of the valley and enough mandarin to prevent the perfume from magnolia blandness.. Moonmilk is beautiful and flickering, befitting the glow of its namesake in the atramental stillness of caves decorated with stalactites and stalagmites, roofs hung with droplets of dissolved stone.. . Composition: . Black Tea, Lime. Cardamom, Lily-of-the-Valley, Mandarin, Black Pepper. Eau de Parfum. . Smoke on the water. A slow low sonic boom. Out of the fog something is heralded by the strange, indecipherable sound of water thunder. This perplexing scent explores the eerie mystery of Mistpouffer, the name given to the aural phenomenon.. The Japanese refer to it as uminari, or cries form the sea, and many theories have been forward as to the cause of the sound, from solar winds, gas bubbles, earthquakes , ghosts and water spirits.. It took Stora Skuggan four years of research before they were happy with Mistpouffer's final composition. Foggy not overtly aquatic, gently smoky and natural, not funereal or spooky. By nature, fog is intangible, ethereal and eerie, something that cannot be captured despite its ability to obfuscate landscapes.. Mistpouffer drifts intimately around a core of immortelle, fig and smoke. The salt-cured liquorice vibe of immortelle is used with skill and awareness of effect. An emerald inflection of pine is wrapped in ozone, aerating the heart. Smoke and the stony enigma of cypriol are the bitter water, enhanced by the damp rootiness of quality vetiver. There is an unexpected note of malt sugar in the base of Mistpouffer, providing a lacteal veneer that is quietly comforting.. Throughout there is a sense of external atmosphere within a tension cloud of erratic weather, and this is tempered by the unpredictable nature of fog, rolling, creeping and veiling. Sounds are muted, and for a moment you are alone with just your beautifully scented skin.. . Composition: . Immortelle, Bergamot. Fig Leaf, Pine, Ozone. Smoke, Vetiver, Malt Sugar, Cypriol. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum, aqua, limonene, linalool, coumarin, eugenol, farnesol, benzyl benzoate, citral, geraniol, benzyl salicylate, citronellol .

Eau de Parfum. . Inky liquorice, bitter wormwood, scraped lichen, dirty flowers, herbs and the black-eyed hex of belladonna and black hemlock. A loamy essay in perfumed darkness. Midnight burials, entheogenic visions and the delicious euphoria of night flight.. The word Hexensalbe means Witches’ Salve or Flying Ointment, a toxic concoction of deadly flora thought to be smeared suggestively on broomsticks and applied transdermally. Containing ingredients like belladonna, mandrake, henbane and jimson weed, the salve caused psychotropic trips due to the atropine and scopolamine present in many of the materials.. Hexensalbe from Stora Skuggan is beautifully disturbing, inspired by this most bizarre mix of deliriants. The perfume is dominated by a chthonic liquorice note dusted with salt, a reference to Salmiaklakrits, a hugely popular form of black liquorice flavoured and sometimes dusted with bitter Salmiak salt.. Rosemary adds a metallic edge, while the musky pepper of angelica, woody lichen and an erotic taint of tuberose create an array of reflective effects. Deadly Nightshade (Atropa Bella-Donna) and black hemlock, allied with the bitter absinthe nuances of Wormwood reference the hallucinogenic Salve.. On skin, it is both macabre and poignant with a slow glassy fade. A scent of occult euphoria and delirious comedown.. . Composition: . Wormwood, Salty Liquorice. Eau de Parfum. . The delicious green snap of stems and crushed leaves introduces the strange world of Fantôme de Maules, perhaps one of the most whimsical perfumes in the Stora Skuggan collection. The whoosh of initial green is beautifully enhanced by the savoury piquancy of bergamot, lime and the mulchy scent of galbanum resin.. Fantôme de Maules is inspired by the eerie urban legend of Le Loyon in Maules, a village in the French-speaking part of Switzerland, an area of forests and rolling agricultural land. Sightings date back to the 1990s and 2000s of a mysterious tall figure dressed in a boiler suit, an old camouflage cloak and a vintage GP-5 gas mask. It all sounds rather sinister, but Le Loyan posed no threat, in fact quite the opposite, he was quiet, skittish and made every attempt to stay away from other people. If glimpsed, he was looking at plants and flowers, content in his forest environment.. Then in 2013, Le Matin published an unambiguous image of the Fantôme that changed everything. Soon after, his carefully folded cloak was discovered in the woods, gas mask on top and a note from Le Loyon saying the photograph has destroyed his ability to continue being himself and the publicity might impact the eco-balance of the forest. This was the last contact from this strange figure.. He is the most wonderful inspiration for a perfume and Stora Skuggan has created something that smells surreal and elusive, using materials that connect and camouflage with Le Loyan’s beloved landscapes like his legendary cloak.. After the delightful bright green opening, there is a musky engaging swell of coriander, forest flowers, cardamom and the bruised purple of lavender absolute that smells poised and contemplative before sinking into a mossy, woody base with resinous leafy echoes. It is a withdrawal back into the shadows, despite flashes of spice and dewy verdancy, reaffirming its mystery in the face of exposé.. As with all the Stora Skuggan perfumes, the Fantôme de Maules storytelling is idiosyncratic and enigmatic, permitting appreciation of materials and inspiration.. . Composition: . Eau de Parfum. . Azalai is inspired by one of the last remaining salt trade routes in North Africa, specifically used by the Tuareg nomads of the Ténéré desert region of the Southern Sahara. Along this caravan route stood a single acacia tree, the loneliest tree in the world.. The tree was considered unique, and it was generally understood that camels were not to nibble on the leaves or travellers to harvest wood for fires. Astonishingly, in 1973 a drunken truck driver crashed into it and killed it. An ignominious end.. Azalai is a perfume of gold, sun and expanses of shifting sands illuminated by the honeyed leather of saffron and thirst-quenching blood orange. The erudition and delight of Azalai lies in the olfactory reference points of this trade route history reflected in the notes and accords of the perfume: tea, spices like cardamon, pepper nutmeg and clove, dried fruit, textiles and glittering gold.. Saffron, blood orange and warm amber are the sun’s constant presence and mint references the sweet hot mint tea drunk at night around a fire. An interesting note is gum acacia, an exudation of the acacia tree that has a soft scent of roasted marshmallows, it is a subtle compliment to the more lingering incense note and leathered dried fruits.. The key to the lingering atmospherics of Azalai is the use of Velvione, a synthetic musk that has an exalting powdered effect that diffuses around the other materials, smoothing, creating a soft-focus sillage resembling the slow fall of heated day into night.. . Composition: . Blood Orange, Mint. Saffron, Dried Fruit. Amber, Incense, Gum Acacia, Velvione. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum, aqua, limonene, alpha-isomethyl ionone, linalool, coumarin .

EXTRAIT DE PARFUM. . There is delicious magic at play in Idìlios, the sixth perfume from Andrea Bissoli Rubini and uber-talented perfumer Cristiano Canali at Rubini Profumi. It follows on from the eerie metal-dusted rocket after-burn of Hyperion, one of the most original compositions to launch in recent years. Idìlios is a sequel to Hyperion, the unanchored sweet drift of hazy mission, the aftermath of orbit arrival.. A serenity of intense notes evoking the soft-scoop memories of a hush-hush love affair, Idìlios is a delicate, yet impactful blend of musks, vanillas, velveteen peach, green tea, coconut, osmanthus and the honeyed ivory sensuality of champaca flower. Mandarine and bergamot are suspended at the top, radiating a secretive pastel light.. There are no weak links in Andrea and Cristiano’s output; from the chalky wine eroticism of Fundamental, through coffee and woods of Tambour Sacré, burning rubber and racing gasoline of Nuvolari, sci-fi bucolic idyll of Odenaturae, Hyperion and now Idìlios. Six visionary perfumes sparking synapses and involuntary memories.. ‘Idìlios is for those who have been through the storm and find calm.’. These words from the Rubini website capture perfectly the soothing emergence into clarity through the lactonic haze of Idìlios that makes it so unique.. There is beautiful boldness in combing a milky peach note with a pastel imagining of aerated candyfloss. Layering this with the dense honeyed tuberose tones of champaca, snowy osmanthus and green tea make Idìlios so compelling; it is joyous to find a perfume you want to wear and wear. It smells beautiful sprayed on clothes and hair, creating an intangible aura of mystery and comfort.. Interestingly there are three different extractions of vanilla, each one adding a slightly different nuance of cassonade. The lacteous refreshment of coconut serves to exalt the inherent alabaster drift of Idìlios and provides another whorl of enigma into this opaque and strange synthesis of olfactive reverie.. . Recently, perfumer Diane St. Clair re-discovered Barbara Kruger’s “Untitled (Your Body is a Battleground)” created for the 1989 March for Women’s Lives in Washington D.C. For St. Clair, this iconic protest art is as relevant today as it was then.. After 50 years of legal protection for reproductive rights after Roe v. Wade, these protections were nullified with the 2022 Dobbs decision. This has resulted in many states outlawing women’s right to choose. Amidst these setbacks, the specter of growing contempt for women reared its ugly head again after the shocking case in France of Gisele Pelicot. Police discovered that Pelicot’s husband, over the span of a decade, routinely drugged her and invited strangers to join him in raping her. These men defended their actions, saying that they assumed her husband could grant them permission for such acts.. Diane has created two perfumes, Armor and Sanctuary, to use the art of scent — and its power to provoke our deepest emotions — to speak out against a culture that allows men to control women’s bodies without their consent. She hopes that wearing these perfumes can provide a sense of both empowerment and security.. Alex Musgrave notes that the power and disturbed beauty of Sanctuary lies in its “smells and dreams of longing, an odd bitterness of feeling trapped in a life that has slowly, corrosively taken you captive.” . Slowly being taken captive is how it can feel to lose gender equality, reproductive rights, and body autonomy. For many, pregnancy has become dangerous, as doctors fear treating emergency miscarriages in states where abortion is illegal. Likewise, Gisele Pelicot awoke from years of being abused by her husband to see the horrors that had occurred while she was unwittingly held captive.. This fragrance is intimate and spectral. It speaks of pollen and flowers, rich fruits, and moist greenery. Streaked like a watercolor painting, its beauty is akin to opening a window in spring. It offers calm and quiet, creating a protective sanctuary to heal and survive.. Armor and Sanctuary are conceptual fragrances designed to evoke a feeling without a disclosed list of notes or materials used to create them. . Perfumer: Diane St. Clair, 2025.

The Blue Marble is the photograph of Earth, taken in 1972, by the crew of Apollo 17 on their way to the Moon. Showing the Earth’s vulnerability and isolation in the vastness of space, it quickly became an iconic symbol of environmental activism for generations.. Another symbol of our Earth, named after the Greek goddess Gaia, created much attention with its own hypothesis. The Gaia hypothesis, proposed in the 1970’s by scientists James Lovelock and Lynn Margulis, contends that Earth is an enormous ecosystem, comprised of many smaller systems. Together, they represent a dynamic and self regulating process in which oceans, atmosphere, plants, animals, fungi and the Earth’s crust, interact to maintain and adjust conditions for life to exist on the planet. This theory has informed emerging hypotheses such as earth system science, which takes a holistic approach to how geology, oceanography, ecology, and meteorology all affect the health of the Earth and its ability to sustain life.. These theories and discoveries are increasingly being used to study climate change, in all its facets, and how changes in one ecosystem impact another. As we do this, we realize how susceptible our Earth is to the effects of various man-made pollution, warming and the continued arrogance of humans.. This Blue Marble perfume represents the beauty, complexity and fragility of Earth’s intertwining systems through scent. Comprised of 7 accords representing oceans, soil, cold flowers, wet rocks, woods, green plants and metals, it allows us to think about and experience the intersection of these endangered ecosystems personally, as they move across our skin, through time and space.. Composition: . Marine Notes, Plants, Soil, Stone, Blossoms, Metal, Woods. Edge Effects in ecology are changes in population species that occur when two or more habitat areas border each other. At the edge of these overlapping ecosystems, species from both habitats are found traveling and interacting. The inspiration for St. Clair's two perfumes, Pandora and Eve, is the painting “Pandora” (1896) by the Pre-Raphaelite artist, John William Waterhouse.. Showing Pandora as she opens the forbidden box, the artist captures her curious, innocent expression against the backdrop of a dark, sinister forest. The stories of Pandora and Eve, who reached for the forbidden apple, have much in common. Both came to symbolize women who were punished for disobeying orders and acting on their impulses towards curiosity.. St. Clair believe that women who challenge the rules and follow their curiosity are striving towards creativity, innovation and independence. Thus, these perfumes are part of St. Clair's “Audacious Innocence” collection.. Pandora and Eve are “sister” formulas, sharing most of the same notes. The inspiration for St. Clair's two perfumes, Pandora and Eve, is the painting “Pandora” (1896) by the Pre-Raphaelite artist, John William Waterhouse.. Showing Pandora as she opens the forbidden box, the artist captures her curious, innocent expression against the backdrop of a dark, sinister forest. The stories of Pandora and Eve, who reached for the forbidden apple, have much in common. Both came to symbolize women who were punished for disobeying orders and acting on their impulses towards curiosity.. St. Clair believe that women who challenge the rules and follow their curiosity are striving towards creativity, innovation and independence. Thus, these perfumes are part of the St. Clair “Audacious Innocence” collection.. Composition: . Apple Accord, Cedrat, Bergamot, Red Mandarin, Tomato leaf. EAU DE PARFUM. . NOT INNOCENT is an indulgent patisserie romp inspired by a much-loved Croatian pastry called Rožata; rich with caramelised vanilla and rose petals.. Composed by Olivier Cresp, it is a moreish gourmand that doesn't have any of the sticky artificial afterburn often left by many cheaper sweet scents. Many smell delicious at first but fade to hollow or overtly sweet.. Cresp has used orange, almond and a dash of rum in the top notes. Toffee-flavoured milk and rose provide a swirling, unctuous heart with creamy vanilla and the spiced, sweet hay vibe of tonka bean, which exalts the vanilla and almond, creating delicate patisserie layers of aroma.. "I was inspired by a Croatian pastry that the brand's founder introduced me to when we met: Rožata.. I wanted to recreate into a non-sticky, gourmand fragrance with a warm, sensual, creamy and addictive drydown embodied by vanilla, milky notes and oakmoss.". Olivier Cresp. Composition: . Almond, Orange, Rum. Toffee, Milk Smell-the-TasteTM, Rose Essence. Vanilla, Sandalwood, Tonka Bean, Oakmoss. EAU DE PARFUM. . I AM is a sparkling and luminous bouquet of freesias, magnolia, lit by solar orange blossom and the quiet glow of peonies.. Created by Nathalie Lorson, who tempers any suggestion of floral excess with deft additions of mandarin and piquant pink pepper that always adds textured radiance. A brace of airy musks, balsamic benzoin and milky sandalwood anchor the flowers to skin with grace and subtlety.. Patience, a light touch and time taken to understand that the layers should open like petals will seduce and delight. I AM is a chic and long-lasting scent that smells beautiful.. "I wanted to create an image of assertive, confident, multi-faceted femininity.. To achieve this, I chose fresh and sparkling Mandarin Essence and Pink Pepper to capture Croatian light and energy.. For the heart, I imagined a rich, radiant bouquet of Magnolia, Orange Blossom and Peony to express a freedom and confidence.. For the base notes, I combined the sophistication of Cedar, addictive Benzoin and the comfort of Musk for a fragrance that is resolutely sensual, sophisticated, and memorable.". Nathalie Lorson, perfumer. . Composition: . Mandarin Essence of Italy, Freesia, Pink Pepper Supercritical Fluid Extraction. Magnolia, Orange Blossom, Peony. Cedarwood, Benzoin Resin, Musks. EAU DE PARFUM. . DSCVR ME! is a take on the popular fresh marine, oceanic style, created to pay homage to the famously clear azure waters off the Dalmatian coast.. Made by Olivier Cresp, who has brought his years of experience to bear on an addictive, mineralised mix of seawater effects, pungent eucalyptus, liquorice-scented, masala spiced immortelle all stylishly counterpointed with a wind-swept jasmine, anisic mastic and a rush of crisp ambroxan that fills DSCVR ME! with coastal lift and breeze.. "DSCVR ME! embodies an original, vertical freshness with resinous and salty notes.. I was inspired by the emerald sea and the rocks of the Dalmatia region.. To transcribe the smell of this grandiose landscape, I choose immortelle for its salty side, embodying sea spray, and mastic, native to the Mediterranean basin, for its resinous tones.. Olivier Cresp, Perfumer. . Composition: . Italian Bergamot, Eucalyptus Buds, Immortelle Absolute. Salty Marine Accord, Jasmine Absolute, Mastic Absolute. Ambrox, Musk, Oak Moss. EAU DE PARFUM. . I’Khana is a word from the Choctaw language meaning enlightened, and this beautiful perfume is one of bright luminescence and warm breezes over the Florida Keys.. The opening is beautifully zesty and bitter-sweet, with grapefruit, a notoriously difficult note to use in perfume, bright and joyful as holiday laughter. A zephyr of salty air and tropical light is washed through with sharp woody lime rind that serves to further exalt the pithy rush of opening citrus.. A generous dose of sparkling pink pepper bridges the wilful top notes into an acerbic and earthy blast of ginger absolute that balances moist pungency with earthy woodiness reflecting the rhizome’s underground origins.. Everything about I’Khana celebrates refreshment and a cool peace of mind. Interestingly the citrus notes, while softening, have lovely staying power, fading down into a base creamy sandalwood, coconut and a diffusion of skin-soft white musks.. The result is simultaneously calming and dynamic, not overtly intrusive but blended so well, the notes sink into the skin with laid-back sensuality.. As with all the Source Adage perfumes there is a soft tension in the way I’Khana unfolds and eases itself out on skin making it feel like an intimate part of you.. . Composition: . Zesty Grapefruit, Lime Rind, Pink Pepper. Ginger, Cardamom. Sandalwood, Coconut, Pale Musk. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Parfum (Fragrance), Limonene, Pinene, Pelagronium Graveolens Flower Oil, Tetramethyl Acetyloctahydronaphthalenes, Citrus Aurantium Flower Oil, Terpineol, Citronellol, Linalool, Pogostemon Cablin Oil, Linalyl Acetate, Geraniol, Terpinolene, Geranyl Acetate, Citral, Beta-Caryophyllene, Farnesol .

EAU DE PARFUM. . aka’ula is a native Hawaiian word meaning red sunset, fitting for a perfume inspired by rumbling volcanic activity. The original version of the perfume has been updated with the addition of a marine accord and using upcycled materials.. It is one of the most atmospheric perfumes in the collection, delicately mineralised, a scent of hot stones and bubbling cold springs with a moist marine algae note enhanced by citrus and ginger.. Hawaii is well known for its pineapples; they have long been an important export from the islands. The crushed grassiness of pineapple leaves wafts through the heart of aka’ula, boosted by a carefree vetiver note. The volcanic nuances of the perfume are there from the start, but only really become fumed reality as a flinty oud and smoke scenario begin to billow through the composition. Softened by vanilla, the smoky Paynes Grey tonality fades into a cold drift of oceanic tranquillity rolling over dark rocks and algal pools.. Red suggests fire and lava, and while aka’ula is a striking perfume, the smoke, sea-hiss and charred air of vulcanology are smudged and delicate, a mood you can wrap around yourself and slip into a hazy, lazy trance.. . Composition . Spicy Ginger CO2 Extract, Pineapple Leaves. Coffee, Smoke. Vetyver, Agarwood, Vanilla. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Parfum (Fragrance), Tetramethyl Acetyloctahydronaphthalenes, Acetyl Cedrene, Juniperus Virginiana Oil, Pogostemon Cabin Oil, Linalool, Cedrus Atlantica Oil / Extract, Citronellol, Eugenyl Acetate, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Limonene, Citrus Lemon Peel Oil, Benzyl Benzoate, Coumarin, Citrus Aurantium Peel Oil, Linalyl Acetate, Beta-Caryophyllene, Pinene, Terpineol, Citral .

listings.rawTitle: TEA & ROCK N ROLL Full Size 75ml | 2.5oz
listings.description: EAU DE PARFUM. . This delicious perfume is inspired by the bergamot-infused taste and aroma of Earl Grey tea swirling through nostalgic echoes of Carnaby Street, Bailey, The Shrimp, Mick Jagger, Twiggy, The Who, Mary Quant and Dusty. Larger than life boys and girls who pushed at the boundaries of life, sex, fashion, drugs and musical innovation. It was an era of dandified fashion, Mods and a rejection of the until then huge influence of American music.. This fusion of music, art, fashion and the cult of personality has never really been equalled, not with the same ferocity and commitment to cause and effect. There was also a distinctive mood of fun and frivolity, not taking things too seriously, combining the British fascination with eccentricity, class, feral beauty and hardcore living, burning millions of candles at so many ends. Tea & Rock n Roll plays with our perceptions of this time, an era now so immersed in nostalgia it is hard to extrapolate reality.. A fantasy sure, but the perfumed construct is simple and evocative. Earl Grey tea is seen as quintessentially British, sipped from porcelain cups, the senses immersed in the mouthfeel of black tea leaves infused with pieces of bergamot peel, one of the perfume world’s most utilised materials. A hybrid of lime and lemon, bergamot is deeply aromatic and appears in an overwhelming percentage of perfumes, usually as a top or head note with other citrus notes and herbs.. The bergamot in Tea & Rock n Roll is beautifully supported by yerba maté, well known as a beverage in South America, brewed from the leaves of a plant in the holly genus. As a perfume note it imparts a mown grassy greenness with hints of leather and sweet hay. Tonka bean is the lovely rounded vanillic note in the base, creating a smooth, woozy fade to the stylish combination of notes.. Tea & Rock n Roll is a witty, chic perfume, managing to be both ephemeral and tangibly sensual. The Earl Grey vibe is just delicious and reminiscent of golden smoky tea with a slice of lemon gently spinning in the steam. Herbaceous and sweet, zesty and dreamy, the concept of languid dandyism is alive and smelling sublime.. . Composition: . Lime, Bergamot. Maté. Leather, Tonka Bean. Perfumer: Camille Goutal, Isabelle Doyen, 2020. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance), Limonene*, Linalool*, Geraniol*, Citral*, Citronellol*, Coumarin*, Benzyl Benzoate*, Benzyl Alcohol*, Eugenol* (Alcohol from organic farming. * Made from ingredients of natural origin.) .

EAU DE PARFUM. . Grand Jeu has a few different meanings but the one that seems to suit this dazzling white floral, oozing luxurious beach chic is to the reference to a specific combination of full throttle stops on the French organ.. Le Grand Jeu reverberates with playful and languorous sensuality. Warm holiday skin, glistening with Ambre Solaire, golden traces of sand across bronzed bodies. Then it segues into a deeper evening vibe.. The opening blast of gardenia and tuberose is like walking into dazzling sunlight from a chilled hotel lobby, cold marble under foot. There is a gentle sea breeze and the scent of tropical greenery. Le Grand Jeu has a delicious air of chic privacy about it, a secret beach with hushed visitors under discreet parasols radiating exclusivity.. The ocean breathes gently over the sand, rustling leaves and branches further inland. Everything feels slowed down and suspended in gauzy sensuality, the glorious white floral notes blended with milky coconut and a shimmering veil of vanilla. Le Grand Jeu is a beautiful combination of hypnotic blooms and creamy vacation serenity. A perfume with the deliberate grace of a single baroque pearl on a gold chain resting on skin, the whiteness flickering with gold from sun-kissed skin.. . Composition: . Coconut Milk. Gardenia, Tuberose. Vanilla. Perfumer: Camille Goutal, Isabelle Doyen, 2020. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance), Limonene*, Linalool*, Benzyl Salicylate*, Geraniol*, Citral*, Citronellol*, Eugenol*, Benzyl Alcohol*, Coumarin*, Benzyl Benzoate*, Farnesol* (Alcohol from organic farming . * made from ingredients of natural origin.) .

EAU DE PARFUM. . A Mediterranean holiday in a bottle. L’Echappée Sauvage translates roughly as Wild Getaway, implying off the beaten track vacations, the fantasy of isolation and the suspension of time. Perfumery is a fantasy in its own obsessive and immersive way, conjuring memories, suggesting times, places, lovers and experiences. Allying these to fictional encounters and destinations, the main inspiration behind the Voyages Imaginaires line.. L’Echappée Sauvage is essentially a fig perfume, piquant with lemon, bergamot and sparkling pink pepper. Terpenic green notes conjure the heady summer redolence of Stone pines, while cedar wood and the smoky beauty of guaiac wood deepen the sense of being hidden and at ease with your surroundings. The moreish leathered sweetness of tonka bean rounds off the overall quality and beauty of the sap-green figgy milkiness. The overall effect is one of restrained yet immersive beauty, hints of saline breeze and drifting sand.. L’Echappée Sauvage is a distinctively southern mediterranean scent, fig has become olfactive shorthand for sun-soaked terraces, lazy beach visits and drinking chilled aperitifs under dappled leaf shade. This lush Voyages Imaginaires perfume is indulgent and perfectly private. You feel enriched by its beauty.. . Composition: . Bergamot, Fig, Lemon, Pink Pepper. Almond, Narcissus. Cedar, Clary Sage, Gaiac Wood, Tonka Bean. Perfumer: Camille Goutal, Isabelle Doyen, 2020. . Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance), Limonene*, Linalool*, Citral*, Coumarin*, Geraniol*, Isoeugenol*, Citronellol* (Alcohol from organic farming.* made from ingredients of natural origin.) .

EAU DE PARFUM. This punning title, a play on immortal and immortelle, is a pungent, golden blend of fragrant elemi resin, benzoin, labdanum and of course a generous dose of immortelle or helichrysum. Amber and bergamot work together beautifully, creating a bright lacquering effect flecked with gold.. This is a tinder dry perfume, reminiscent of scorched vegetation, the legendary Maquis of the southern mediterranean, a torrid composition of flayed sweetness that might ignite at any moment. In fact, Amyris, which produces the elemi resin is sometimes referred to as torchwood, as the sap and exudation are highly flammable and have been known to spontaneously combust and burn for hours.. It is the immortelle with its off-kilter floral sweetness and curried liquorice scent that defines Eau des Immortels, oscillating as it does between singed gorse, cumin and tobacco-tinted vanilla.. The perfume smells volatile, tension between the resins and charismatic immortelle plays out gently but resonantly. There is a key base note of chocolate, which serves to hold everything together, a dark cocoa mood under the panoply of resins. It resembles a sweeter, more suggestive patchouli and as the perfume develops, asserts itself beautifully with the savoury smoulder of the immortelle.. Eau des Immortels is a picturesque, jazzy riff on a familiar, some say divisive material, but it is further proof that Camille Goutal and Isabelle Doyen have a profound understanding of natural materials and work olfactive magic.. Composition: . Bergamot. Immortelle, Amyris. Benzoin, Chocolate, Labdanum, Vanilla. Perfumer: Camille Goutal, Isabelle Doyen, 2022. inci list: Alcohol Denat, Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance), Limonene*, Linalool*, Coumarin*, Citronellol*, Citral*, Benzyl Benzoate*, Geraniol*, Eugenol*, Farnesol*, Isoeugenol*, Benzyl Alcohol*. (Alcohol from organic farming. * Made from ingredients of natural origin.) .

listings.rawTitle: LA COULEUR DE LA NUIT Full Size 75ml | 2.5oz
listings.description: EAU DE PARFUM. . Soundtracked by swooning melancholic strings, a beautiful woman wearing an exquisite silk cheongsam sways sensually through quiet 1960’s back streets under flickering streetlights. She is carrying a jade green enamelled food pail and seems almost too beautiful to be real, her cat-flick eyes and immaculate hair, body emboldened by the exquisite silk.. This is a description of Maggie Cheung in In the Mood for Love, directed by visionary auteur Wong Kar Wai, one of the most sublime films ever made. A story of slow burning desire between two people who suspect their respective spouses are having an affair. In languid consideration of how this might have unfolded, they inadvertently light a smouldering flame to their own feelings.. The film is about the unsaid, sublimating desire, but this only serves to heighten every look, touch and it is this mise en scene that inspires La Couleur de la Nuit.. Intriguingly it is lavender that gives La Couleur de la Nuit its sultry ambiguity. Used with skill and imagination it can sing a potent song of bruised indigo.. Camille and Isabelle have used the lavender as a twilight colour wash, seared at the edges and shadowed. It acts like the shadowy streets of late night desire. It is perfectly complimented by rose geranium, one of the most beautiful materials used by perfumers, the rubbed green furry softness of the leaves and the smudged rose facet that develops so elegantly on skin.. Both materials are wrapped in a voluptuous vanilla note, orchidaceous and unctuous, echoing the Tahitian childhood of Isabelle Doyenne. Fir balsam is a fascinating addition to the composition of La Couleur de la Nuit. It provides a green hue of abandonment to perfumes, a whiff of burnt churches in arctic forests. It smells like ghosts and secrets. Anchored in a cocoa-leaning patchouli, this beautiful perfume captures the colour of twilight assignations and enigmatic blooming of love.. . Composition . Lavender. Bergamot, Geranium. Fir Balsam, Patchouli, Vanilla. EAU DE PARFUM. . The name of this gorgeous moreish perfume is Arabic for orange tree, and Azahar delivers a thirst-quenching rush of citrus over a base of marshmallow soft vanilla. It smells silvered, suggesting Moroccan riads with their enclosed courtyards and gardens, fountains delicately flowing in the fragrant air, contrasting with street heat and arid air.. Azahar is a silken scent, walking a delicate line between lush orange and vanillic comfort. There is a culinary tradition in North African and Mediterranean cuisine of adding orange flower water to both sweet and savoury dishes. Powdered sugar is used too, adding a rich and unexpected facet. Salads, pastries, tagines can all be given a twist with floral waters. Azahar dips into this tradition by combining heady orange blossom, petit-grain and tangerine served over a base of pillowy vanilla, whose orchid origins seem to be underlined by the orange blossom and zesty citrus. The mix of piquant carnality and solar yearning make for memorable wearing.. Using combinations of citrus notes, like the sweeter tangerine and pithy green of petit-grain with the indolic orange will ease out the longevity and embedding it in a marshmallow soft vanilla creates a languorous and exalted epilogue. Azahar is beautiful to wear, a beautifully crafted citric floral that can be worn from day into delicious night.. . Composition: . Bergamot, Tangerine, Petit Grain. Orange Blossom, Tuberose. Marshmellow, Vanilla. Perfumer: Camillle Goutal, Isabelle Doyen, 2020. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Aqua (Water), Parfum (Fragrance), Linalool*, Limonene*, Geraniol*, Citral*, Citronellol*, Farnesol*, Benzyl Alcohol*, Benzyl Benzoate* (Alcohol from organic farming. * Made from ingredients of natural origin.) .

Eau de Parfum. . Comme un Gant literally fits the skin like a bespoke glove perhaps in fine silk or butter soft kid leather. It is a milky take on the suede/leather genre, built beautifully around an unctuous coconut and Madagascan vanilla pairing. Rather than an expected tropical vibe, the creamy body is studded with the piquancy of aromatic cardamom. Haitian vetiver in the base adds a damp grassy rootiness, imparting freshness and atmosphere to the composition.. All of the Voyages Imaginaires perfumes have a distinctive mood as a result of Camille and Isabelle’s commitment to be 100% natural, and the wheatgerm alcohol lends a silken tenderness to the perfumes on skin. It allows the coconut in Comme un Gant to develop an elegant swirling nuttiness and beautifully compliment the lacteous sandalwood in the base notes.. There is an indefinable immaculacy about Comme un Gant, a languid nod to tropical gourmand perfumes and the nostalgic aroma of holiday skin. The shift from languid, spiced coconut milk through opaque woods to a sumptuous vanilla is delicately yet assertively handled. The quiet inclusion of Haitian vetiver with its subtle touches of citrus and floral amongst the aromatic green make for a satisfying ending, both fixing and exalting the sensual fit of Comme un Gant.. . Composition: . Cardamom, White Peach. Coconut, Iris, Vanilla. Suede, Musk, Sandalwood, Vetiver. Extrait Absolu Perfume Oil. . Eau de Parfum. . "My work has always involved the human body, its social identity, how it communicates, how it is represented." - Briac Frocrain, founder of Marlou. The hélio part of this unsettling and addictive new perfume from Marlou nods at the sunlit voyeurism of vacations by azure pools.. Héliodose, composed by the talented Stéphanie Bakouche gives us sweat-glossed flesh, indolent heat and the sensuality of Jonathon Glazer’s ominously sensual film Sexy Beast. As always with Marlou perfumes, the beauty of the complex fragrances lies in the combination of prurience and fantasies.. There is a humid fecundity to Héliodose, the name hinting subconsciously at overdose. It is a perfume of slick hot skin, lying in hot still grass with a lover, words unnecessary, fingers brushing electric and moist. The body is a flower, its purpose to attract desire.. An unexpected base of gold-tooled bookbinding crumbling over time provides a pomaded anchorage of green galbanum, tiaré and musky indoles. There is disturbance throughout Héliodose, a sense of what is smelled is not in fact the full story. Can perfumes be menacing? The answer is yes, and Marlou is a brand exploring this with off kilter beauty.. Héliodose brings to mind Jacques Demy’s 1969 film La Piscine, starring Alain Delon and Romy Schneider, with a young Jane Birkin as the beguiling ingenue. Shneider and Delon had had a very public and difficult break up, but Delon was obsessed and wanted her back, demanding to Demy she be cast in La Piscine or he wouldn’t do it either. It led to palpable erotic tension on set in a film already immersed in sun-soaked jealousy.. As befitting a film about vacation indolence and sexual suspense, there is a lot of sunbathing, an activity that seems to exist purely to elicit the erotic gaze. Marlou’s Héliodose is the scent-track to Demy’s film, a perfume that simmers with humid want and weaponised skin. It is another triumphant composition for Briac Frocrain’s inimitable brand.. . Composition: . Galbanum, Tiaré, Indole, Musk. Perfumer: Stéphanie Bakouche, 2025. Artistic direction: Briac Frocrain.

Eau de Parfum. . I created Marlou so that, from an olfactory perspective, the body could take its place in society. This implies the acceptance and even ownership of faults, of imperfections inherent to that living object which is never wholly clean. - Briac Frocrain, founder of Marlou. In many ways, all of the Marlou perfumes are preoccupied with the hidden intricacies of the human body, the begrimed, dishevelled and salacious. Pretty has no place at the Marlou table and if there are traces of it, it serves only to lure you into experiencing a more profound and unexpected world of odiferous transgression.. Doliphor is a quiet thing at the start, but probes at the senses like a tongue at a nagging tooth. The rising oddness transmutes into an off-kilter fairytale of fragrant flesh, the body fitted to fabric and leaving an imprint of exertion and decoration, hazy with laundry musks and the comforting wheaten scent given off by warm clean skin.. Like a personal manifestation of the Turin Shroud, Doliphor seems to drape exquisitely over the body and then lift slightly, allowing a light breeze to play over skin. The ingredients coalesce into a milky gauze and moist bathroom vibe of steamed mirror, damp towels, air moist with lacteous ablutions. Carrot seed adds a dusting of earthy powder with traces of costus and cumin laced through to create a subtle whiff of settling sweat and hair.. Doliphor comes together with disturbing grace, a genuinely addictive perfume, a second skin, a veiling of accumulated odours that plays with fetishist tropes while wooing mind and electric body with delicate suggestions of nuzzling worship.. . Composition: . Saliva, Wheat Flower. Bath towel, Milky veil. Carrot seed, Costus, Cumin, Musk. Perfumer: Emma Lehaut, 2025.

Extrait de Parfum. . The word eshal translates as flower of paradise, the perfect name for the latest addition to the Neela Vermeire Créations collection. As usual, Eshal is the work of Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, responsible for Neela’s working through a resonant selection of Indian history, faith, exploration and the sensory complexities of Indian flora and cuisine.. Eshal is a very beautiful and surprising perfume. Throughout the Neela Vermeire Créations line, the scents are enhanced by the inclusion of materials that reflect the marriage of Indian culture and the French perfume classicism beloved by Neela.. Eshal is perfume as parure, fitting as tuberose blooms are often used in the floral leis. It is one of the finest perfumes Bertrand has yet created, a fascinating blend of opulent blooms and a truly obsessively beguiling turmeric - cinnamon duet.. These two spice oils utterly transform the floral experience of the tuberose and radiant citrus notes in the opening salvo of red mandarin, bitter orange, lime and petitgrain. Beeswax absolute adds a subtle but noticeable animalic and pheromonic smear as a lovely Peru balsam and tactile labdanum add just the right amount of sweetened leather.. Eshal is a magnificent achievement, presenting tuberose, an often-divisive flower in a novel and thought-provoking way. Pungency and tenderness combine, and the notes lead to a cosmic, sultry sunset of daring floral satisfaction.. . Composition . Red Mandarin, Bitter Orange, Lime, Petit Grain. tuberose Absolute, Cinnamon Oil, Turmeric Oil. Beeswax Absolute, Peru Balsam, and Labdanum Absolute. Perfumer: Bertrand Duchaufour, 2025.

EAU DE PARFUM. . The name comes from the Croatian dialect of the Carolina Algonquians meaning, Great Spirit. Monto’ac is inspired by smudging, the purification and spiritual cleansing rituals of many First Nation North American peoples, involving the burning of herbs and woods. The smoke is used to penetrate the psyche, the air and carry away any bad resonances. This reflects the original etymology of perfume, per fumum, meaning through smoke.. Monto’ac opens appropriately on a wondrous whoosh of purifying silver sage, one of the omni-present materials in smudging bundles. Sage is a strange botanical, soapy, spicy, charred and slippery. One of the most distinctive herbs in a garden, care must be taken when cooking with, like rosemary it can overwhelm a meal. Yet this overdose is exactly what is required in smudging, a pungent sense of smoke penetrating the very molecules and chasing away ill-will through blessing and cleansing.. A note of muscadine grapes, an American juicy robust variety is an unusual addition, lending grassy rhubarb and Verdejo wine nuances to the composition. This subtle tartness is fumed with green tobacco, quite different from the regular variety, imparting a subtle odour of tomato leaf that works beautifully with the grapes and sage. Oakmoss and a supple suede effect smooth out a haunting drydown with careworn musks stretching Monto’ac through soothed senses.. . Composition: . Silver Sage, Lavender. Muscadine Grape, Green Tobacco Leaves. Leather, Musk, Oakmoss. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum (fragrance), benzyl benzoate, citral, citronellol, coumarin, eugenol, hexyl cinnamal, limonene, linalool .

EAU DE PARFUM. C’i’aan is a gelid whorl of perfumed air, beautifully chilled, a striking capture of that breathtaking moment of stepping out of a warm, protected enclave and plunging into weather that grips like a vice. Mint, especially spearmint can be a divisive note in perfumery, loaded with associations of toothpaste, salads, gum and associated breath freshening things. But used sparingly and wisely with attention to how it sits within other materials it can be uniquely beautiful.. Spearmint has a sweeter, more rounded profile than the mint we are more familiar with, the tabbouleh, lamby condiment one. In this fascinating Source Adage perfume, the spearmint is clarifyingly fresh, conjuring up ice shot through with dormant algae and bubbles of trapped frozen air. Allied to a gamy, gin & tonic rush of juniper, the effect is dramatic without being in any way overpowering.. This sets the scene for a muffled wave of phantom fir trees and icy water tugging gently at moist sand. C’i’aan is a complex build of landscaped legend, hinting at a mosaic of pathways and ceremonial odours played out across a set of dazzling arctic accords tinged hauntingly by the smell of apple skin and quenching flow of raw juice.. The Source Adage perfumes have elegant dry-downs that move through landscapes and time to beautiful effect. It is a big ask of perfumes to present difference in this saturated un-secret world. But like discovering a new writer whose prose or poetry intimately draws you in, C’i’aan is a sublime experience.. . Composition: . Fir Needle, Spearmint. Juniper CO2 Extract, Green Apple. Cedar, Amber. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum (fragrance), benzyl benzoate, citral, eugenol, limonene, linalool .

EAU DE PARFUM. . This scent is the epitome of storm. Everything about it trembles with an uneasy presage of shattering tempest punctuated by those eerie lulls where everything seems to drop to the ground in waiting to speak to rain. Storms have odours. All over the world, cloudbursts, cyclones, squalls and windstorms have an atmospheric and dazzling range of associated smells.. Ki’lei is the immersive perfume of a sudden storm ravishing fir trees, thrashed needles and damp soil hurling scent into the molecules of electrified air.. Ki’lei means cloud in the Yawelmani dialect of Central California and while the idea of clouds having scent is a supremely abstract concept, it is the implied and imaginative idea of texture, surround and experience that matters. How we think different clouds might smell. The glowering, low-darkness of storm clouds are atramentally beautiful, sometimes sudden, skies blackening in a heartbeat or a glow mustering of greys as the air dampens.. Many animals sense storms before humans, we probably could at one time, but like so many primal abilities we once needed, such gifts have been lost to evolving time.. The silver fir note in Ki’lei is redolent with poetic verdancy, the green of it cool and comforting. Pine and fir tree forests have a unique quietude, a softness that embraces. The ground is gentle underfoot and every movement made produces an opposing olfactive reaction. Rosemary, the scent of remembrance, black pepper, cold smoke and the Argentine lustre of metallic aldehydes add to the wild time-capsule of mountainous forests.. What makes Ki’lei so intriguing is the shift three quarters of the way in as the pungent odours of loamy earth rise like fumes from smouldering underworld. Reminiscent of geosmin and freshly turned over beets, it is the perfect finale to electrified skin weather.. . Composition: . Bergamot,Black Pepper, Coriander, Rosemary. Fern, Jasmine Sambac, Lavender,. Silver Fir, Smoke, Mineral-rich Earth.. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum (fragrance), linalool, benzyl benzoate, linalyl acetate, lavandula oil / extract, pinene, hexyl cinnamal, anethole, limonene, tetramethyl acetyloctahydronaphtalenes, pelagronium graveolens flower oil, evernia prunastri (oakmoss) extract, camphor, citronellol, geraniol, beta-caryophyllene, geranyl acetate, terpineol, benzyl alcohol, alpha-terpinene .

EAU DE PARFUM. . The name of this lush, damp floral is derived from an Algonquian word meaning from both sides. Aétai is an atmospheric, immersive portrait of coastal woodland, trees washed with saline moist air. Droplets of soft water suspended from leaves, needles, petal edges, cobwebs, moss and lichen. The shock of salt, a seafarer accord is remarkable, the delicious inhale of briny sea air mingled with flower oxides, woods, wet stones, algae and more sombre moods created by complex accords of dark violet and black walnut.. There is a wind-scoured, pollen-scattered iodine vibe to Aétai, wild iris clinging tenaciously to clifftops, immune to salt and bedded into the soil. In the mix is a parallel mood of old harbour, decaying wood, crumbling boats and rusted moorings. The stones are algae-stained, paths and edges reclaimed by an abundance of flora.. The exhilaration of abandonment is beautiful; a fascinating feature of all the Source Adage perfumes is the implied absence of people, by forced design or just the inherent nature of wilderness.. A gentle mist of ambergris settles over the final drydown in Aétai, lending the perfume a beautifully melancholic ending. A walk along forested shores.. . Composition: . Pink Pepper, Clove, Cape Rose. Wild Iris, Dark Violets, Jasmine Sambac. Sandalwood, Olibanum, Ambergris, Patchouli. . inci list: alcohol denat., parfum (fragrance), benzyl benzoate, citral, citronellol, eugenol, hydroxycitronellal, limonene, linalool .

Eau de Parfum. Ajedrez, the Spanish word for chess is another perfect perfume from Frassaï, the unusual inspiration providing an intricate and contemplative composition that quietly yet profoundly takes the senses on a unique olfactive journey from first moves to a deliciously faded checkmate.. Ajedrez continues perfumer Ralf Schwieger’s love affair with orris, the shimmering, powdered, grey / pink mood material extracted from certain iris bulbs, the roots harvested and stored to maximise the concentration amount of irone in the rhizome, the chemical that gives orris is distinctive, obsessive nature. Ralf created Lipstick Rose for Frédéric Malle, Iris Nazarena for Aedes, and Vanille Insensée for Atelier Cologne, all perfumes that require his beloved iris to be the mysterious masterpieces they are.. The orris extract in Ajedrez is quietly ignited by three key notes of cardamom, black pepper and lavender that combine to bring piquant illumination and bite to the inherent ephemerality of orris.. "Time can move forward, or backward. Time is inverted. Sometimes, it seems to stand still. The pause gains importance. In standing still, there is movement." . Natalia Outeda, Frassaï Founder & Creative Director. This concept works beautifully with Natalia and Ralf’s chess metaphor, the necessary concentrated pauses between moves on the chessboard akin to the absorbing quietuses in the delicious composition of Ajedrez.. Tobacco and ambered woods work softly around the orris vs lavender dynamic, lifting and smudging the notes with mossy hush. The orris in Ajedrez is elegantly arranged, like tender whispers of piano in the background of a summer room. French windows open onto an emerald lawn, curtains gently ruffled by a golden breeze, light flickering over a marble chessboard, pieces on fire in the sun.. . Composition: . Bergamot Essential Oil, Black Pepper Pure Jungle Essence™, Cardamom Pure Jungle Essence™. Orris Extract, Lavender Pure Jungle Essence™. Tobacco, Amber Woods, Labdanum, Moss. Perfumer: Ralf Schwieger, 2025. . inci list: Alcohol Denat., Fragrance (Parfum), Hexyl Cinnamal, Coumarin, Benzyl Benzoate, Citral, Geraniol, Benzyl Alcohol, Citronellol, Cinnamal, Isoeugenol, Eugenol, Hydroxycitronellal, Farnesol, Benzyl Cinnamate .
